title: Step Wharton's big band
summary: Pianist Step Wharton calls him for his big band, which McGhee ranks as the best he had played in, until it breaks up for lack of gigs.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But anyway, when we came back down to Milwaukee, I got a notice from a cat named Step Wharton. Do you know him?
Step Wharton. I've heard of the name.
Anyway, he had a band, a big band. And he needed a trumpet player.
What year is this? Where are we? Are we still in '38?

Yeah, or '39. No, wait a minute. We went to Cincinnati to the Cotton Club, right? Then we went back up to Superior, Wisconsin for six months, and then we came back and then I joined Step. So that would make it about '39 or '40, the early part of '40 maybe. Yeah, I think it was the early part of '40, because shortly after that I went with Jimmy Rochelle in Michigan.
So you kept working your way over.
Well, I had to. That's one thing, you know, if you want to improve yourself, you've got to keep moving wherever you can move. So that's what I did.
I'm with Step Wharton now. This is after...
